A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAMEL study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Corresponding content can be matched despite layout changes and figure renumbering; the appendix pages are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, scaling-law prediction errors, sampling-strategy comparisons and downstream benchmark results, including evaluation on a 55B-A1.2B model.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports numerical loss-improvement ratios in its analysis of capacity allocation.

M1.justification: The CAMEL scaling law, loss-to-benchmark mapping, benchmark-weighted optimization and Hourglass sampling procedure are unchanged. The expanded intrinsic-domain explanation and capacity-allocation analysis do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five training domains, 14 downstream benchmarks, specialized training objectives and Math/Knowledge scenario. The added ratio analysis uses the existing Figure 3 experiment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DML, SODM, the model-size-agnostic method and the human-designed mixture where originally evaluated. The newly cited Olmix work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 2.1 adds a diagnostic metric: the ratio of small-to-large to small-to-medium loss reductions, evaluated at training step 2000. This extends the analysis protocol; existing model scales, data splits, training budgets and benchmark evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the qualitative Figure 3 discussion with a quantitative check of whether effective capacity scales proportionally across domains. The intrinsic-domain ablation, sampling-strategy comparisons and other supplementary analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendices B.1 and B.4 retain the same 20 sampling repetitions and 10 independent runs, respectively, with averaging. The new ratio analysis adds no uncertainty estimates or formal significance test.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports loss-improvement ratios of approximately 2.4 for Math and 4.3 for Knowledge at step 2000. Existing plotted results and benchmark tables are unchanged, including CAMEL's Balanced weighted score of 0.532 in Table 1.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 introduces loss-improvement and ratio definitions and derives the expected ratio under proportional capacity scaling, explaining its similarity across domains with close power-law exponents. Assumption 2.1, Theorem 2.2 and the Appendix D proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about capacity-aware prediction, compute-aware sampling and large-model extrapolation, including 50% optimization-cost savings and benchmark improvements of up to 3%.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains intrinsic domains as latent capability components accommodating validation data with unknown domain composition. It also adds conditional reasoning connecting proportional capacity scaling to similar loss-improvement ratios, while retaining the original dynamic-allocation interpretation.

D1.justification: Architecture, training hyperparameters, mixture construction and fitting details in Appendices A–C are unchanged. The added training-FLOPs wording in Figure 1 and Section 3.2 clarifies compute accounting already documented as 6ND in Appendix B.4; access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2026), Olmix: A framework for data mixing throughout LM development, to the introduction and references. The remaining related-work discussion and positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally expands Section 2.1, makes small grammatical and terminology edits, adds an Impact Statement and replaces the preprint footer with conference publication text. The overall section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 5 exchange numbering, several graphics are enlarged or relocated, and Figure 8 and Table 2 move from page 7 to page 8. Figure 1's caption clarifies the cost measure. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the capacity-allocation motivation more explicit through a defined diagnostic, a conditional derivation and reported Math/Knowledge ratios. The intrinsic-domain explanation also improves clarity. These are limited gains: the central method, benchmark evidence and complete appendices remain unchanged.
